name: English Classical

description.short: Two centuries of English classicism, from Jones and Wren through the Palladian, Georgian, Adam, and Regency phases, transmitted worldwide by pattern book.
description.long:
This family is the single most consequential body of work in the taxonomy for American residential architecture. It establishes the terms — symmetry, bay rhythm, the double-hung sash, storey graduation, the classical entry surround — that American building has been arguing with for three hundred years.

Its historical significance is also methodological. The English carpenter's guide converted architectural design from a guild secret into a purchasable commodity. Gibbs, Langley, Swan, Salmon, and Halfpenny made it possible for a builder who had never seen a correct Ionic order to execute one. That achievement, and its characteristic failure mode — correct details at wrong scales — is the closest historical analogue to what a design platform now attempts.

defining_characteristics: Strict bilateral symmetry and vertically aligned bays
Storey heights graduated rather than equal
The double-hung sash as the governing opening type
Classical apparatus concentrated at the entry and cornice
Pattern-book transmission of correct detail to non-architect builders
